stem: Which one of the following can’t be seen by FAST?
expl: FAST looks for free fluid in the pericardium, hepatorenal (Morison's) pouch, splenorenal recess and pelvis, and shows the solid organs around them. The pancreas is retroperitoneal and poorly seen.

why.A: The splenorenal view shows the spleen.

stem: Proper chest tube insertion location ?

opts.t: 4th intercostal space anterior or mid axillary line

expl: Chest tubes go in the "safe triangle": 4th–5th intercostal space between the anterior and mid-axillary lines (above the rib below, to avoid the neurovascular bundle).

stem: A 50-year-old female Patient was intubated for COVID-19 pneumonia during the round you extubated her and after (2 hours? Not sure) the nurse called you because the patient was hypoxic, using accessory muscles to breathe, paradoxical chest movements, altered mental status. What is the immediate management?

opts.t: positive pressure ventilation and prepare for tracheostomy

expl: Post-extubation respiratory failure (accessory muscles, paradoxical breathing, confusion, hypoxia) → immediate reintubation.

stem: You want to have a correct pressure reading beat to beat and the radial artery can not be accessed, what artery are you going to use?
expl: If the radial artery can't be used for invasive (beat-to-beat) BP monitoring, the next choices are the brachial or femoral artery. Veins can't measure arterial pressure.

why.D: A vein (the femoral ARTERY would be an option).

stem: A 55 y/o man who is receiving total parenteral nutrition through right subclavian central line catheter for short bowel syndrome, developed high temperature (39C). Blood culture was positive staphylococcus aureus. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in management?

opts.t: Remove the catheter and send tip for culture
Change the central line catheter over wire

expl: A catheter-related bloodstream infection with S. aureus → remove the catheter and culture the tip, plus systemic antibiotics. Exchange over a wire keeps the infected tract; fluconazole is for fungi; never treat through an infected line alone.

stem: Patient had a superficial 3cm lipoma on forearm removed, which of the following is the best method for subcuticular skin suturing?

opts.t: 3-0 vicryl, non cutting needle, subcuticular fashion

srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients) Source note (435 A Q3): (Cutting needles are used to suture skin. Davidson), (absorbable suture, such as Monocryl or Vicryl, is used
expl: Skin is closed with a cutting needle; a fine (4-0) absorbable monofilament (Monocryl) in a subcuticular fashion gives the best cosmetic result and needs no removal.

why.A: Non-cutting (round) needles are for soft tissue/bowel; 3-0 Vicryl is braided and thicker.
why.C: Too thick; mattress sutures leave marks.

stem: What is the anatomical landmark that you can use to make sure that you won’t injure the spinal cord with the spinal needle during lumbar puncture?
expl: The line joining the iliac crests (Tuffier's line) crosses L4 (L4/5 space); the cord ends at L1–L2 in adults, so a needle below this level avoids the cord.

stem: Patient presented with sepsis, had a subclavian central line inserted. 2 hours later, he became tachycardic, his BP and O2 saturation dropped, what’s the most likely cause? (incomplete question)
srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients)
expl: Hypotension, tachycardia and desaturation shortly after a subclavian line → iatrogenic tension pneumothorax.

stem: A gentleman was involved in a MVA, he was unrestrained driver, hemodynamically unstable, unconscious, O2 sat 81%. He was not moving any of his limbs. What is the most appropriate next step?

opts.t: Put the patient on the lateral side "recovery position".

expl: Unconscious trauma patient with possible cervical spine injury → open the airway with a jaw thrust (no head tilt).

stem: Which one of the following is done in Foley catheter insertion?

opts.t: Lubricate the tip of the catheter
A size of 24Fr is most commonly used

srcNote: (practical procedures and investigation of surgical patients)
expl: Foley insertion is an aseptic procedure; the catheter tip is lubricated (with lidocaine gel), usually 14–16 Fr in adults, without anaesthesia.

stem: A young female pt underwent simple external hemorrhoidectomy under epidural anesthesia, complaining of headache 24 hrs post-op. Which of the following is not part of the initial management?
srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients)
expl: Post-dural-puncture headache: initial management = bed rest, fluids, analgesics (caffeine). Epidural blood patch is NOT initial; it's for persistent headache.

stem: Patient had superficial 7cm lipoma on the back removed, which of the following is the best method for skin suturing ?
srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients)
expl: Source key A: a monofilament suture in a subcuticular fashion gives the best cosmetic result on the back (the printed "0." gauge is a recall error — skin uses fine sutures such as 3-0/4-0).

why.B: Interrupted non-absorbable sutures leave cross-hatch marks.
why.C: Braided and mattress — not for neat skin closure.
why.D: Braided sutures harbour bacteria; monofilament preferred.

stem: Which of the following is correct regarding Nasogastric tube?

opts.t: Not usually contraindicated in skull base fractures
Insert the tube superiorly into the nose

expl: Placement is confirmed by aspirating gastric contents (pH <5.5) ± X-ray. NG tubes are contraindicated in skull-base fractures, are a clean (not sterile) procedure, and are passed backwards along the nasal floor, not upwards.

stem: Patient had small laceration of his forehead, 5-0 prolene cutting suture were used. the suture should be removed after how many days?
srcNote: (Face 3-5 days) (practical procedures and investigation of surgical patients)
expl: Facial sutures are removed early (3–5 days) because the face is well vascularised and heals fast, and early removal avoids suture marks. The source recalls give 2, 4 and 5 days; the main key is 4 days.

stem: In general precautions, which of the following should be avoided?

opts.t: Sharp instruments discarded in special sharp container
Drapes should be placed in containers
Needles should be resheathed by the same person
Gloves and gown should be removed after all used equipment

srcNote: (Patient safety) (practical procedures & investigations of surgical patients)
expl: Re-sheathing (re-capping) needles is the classic cause of needle-stick injury and must be avoided; sharps go straight into a sharps container.

why.A: This is correct practice, not something to avoid.

stem: A patient presented in the ER with tension pneumothorax undergoing, which of the following is irrelevant?

opts.t: Confirm the chest tube insertion with CT
insert at the level of the nipple, midaxillary
low pressure volume can be useful sometimes

srcNote: (practical procedures and investigation of surgical patient)
expl: Chest-tube placement is confirmed with a chest X-ray, not CT. Asepsis, the 5th ICS at nipple level in the mid-axillary line, and low-pressure suction when needed are all relevant.

stem: Which of the following is not an indication for NGT?
expl: Source key D. The 438 Final keyed perforated duodenal ulcer as NOT an indication (it needs surgery; NGT is only adjunct). Ileus, obstruction and GI bleed are classic indications. Note that 436 Midterm keyed perforated DU AS an indication.

stem: A 28-year-old man with hypovolemic shock due to blunt abdominal injury, require venous cutdown for hemodynamic resuscitation. Which of the following sites is appropriate?
expl: The great saphenous vein lies constantly anterior to the medial malleolus — the classic venous cut-down site in adults.

stem: A 56-year-old man who was admitted to the intensive care unit with septic shock due to complicated diverticulitis underwent internal jugular central venous line insertion. Chest X-RAY has been performed to check for the position of the catheter. Which of the following is the appropriate position of the tip of catheter?
expl: The tip of a CVC should lie in the lower SVC above the right atrium; on CXR this is at the level of the carina (T4–5). In the atrium/ventricle it risks arrhythmia and perforation.

stem: Which of the following is the earliest manifestation of local anesthesia toxicity?
expl: Local anaesthetic toxicity begins with CNS signs: perioral numbness/tingling, metallic taste, tinnitus → confusion, seizures → CVS collapse.

stem: A 56 years old man who was admitted to the intensive care unit with septic shock due to complicated diverticulitis underwent internal jugular central venous line insertion. Chest X-ray has been performed to check for the position of the catheter. Which of the following is the appropriate position of the tip of the catheter?
srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients) Source note (436 A Q14): T4/T5 level, The lower border of 2nd rib or upper border of 3rd rib.
expl: CVC tip should be at the carina level on CXR (lower SVC/cavoatrial junction).

stem: Ideal location for chest tube?

opts.t: 4th intercostal space above 5th rib midaxillary line

expl: Chest tube: 4th/5th intercostal space, above the rib (to spare the neurovascular bundle under the rib above), between the anterior and mid-axillary lines.

why.B: Below the rib injures the neurovascular bundle.

stem: A 48-year-old male had inguinal hernia repair, following his surgery he failed to urinate on his own, following two in and out bladder catheterization he still couldn't urinate. What is the management for this patient’s urinary retention?

opts.t: Discharge home and follow up with urology next week
Observation as this should resolve spontaneously
Insert foley catheter with trial of void in few days

expl: Persistent post-op retention after two in-out catheterizations → indwelling Foley and a trial without catheter in a few days.

stem: A 32-year-old gentleman is a victim of assault and is admitted with multiple injuries including traumatic brain injury and facial fractures. He is admitted to the ICU for further management. The ICU doctor decides to insert a line to monitor blood pressure in a, beat to beat, real time fashion. Where should he/she attempt to insert this line?
expl: The radial artery is the first choice for an arterial line (superficial, collateral flow via the ulnar artery).

stem: Which of the following is not a complication of suprapubic catheter insertion?
expl: Suprapubic catheter risks: infection, bleeding/pelvic vessel injury, bowel perforation — the liver is far away.

stem: Which of the following in not an indication for chest tube insertion?
expl: Chest tubes drain the pleural space (pneumothorax, haemothorax, chylothorax, empyema). Pneumoperitoneum is in the abdomen.

stem: Which of the following is NOT an indication for central catheter
expl: CVC indications: TPN, rapid infusion, vasopressors/irritant drugs, CVP monitoring, poor peripheral access — not routinely for all abdominal surgery.

stem: A patient needed 2 liters of blood and it was given in central line what is the most common complication?
expl: Source key: tension pneumothorax — the most dangerous immediate complication of central venous access (pneumothorax is the classic insertion complication). Infection is commoner later.

stem: Which of the following is the Least common complication for central line insertion ?
expl: Myocarditis isn't a central-line complication; hemothorax, air embolism and infection are.

stem: What is the best position for insertion of suprapubic urinary catheter?

opts.t: Two fingers (4-5 cm) above symphsis pubis
Anterior abdominal wall just above the umbilicus
Anterior abdominal wall just below the umbilicus

srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients)
expl: Suprapubic catheter: midline, about two fingerbreadths (≈ 2–4 cm) above the symphysis pubis, with a distended bladder.

stem: In which of the following conditions is the use of a suprapubic catheter not appropriate?
expl: A suprapubic catheter bypasses the urethra (stricture, injury, bladder-neck obstruction). A ureteric stricture is above the bladder — it needs a stent or nephrostomy.

stem: An 18 years old woman developed urticaria and wheezing following IV injection contrast for abdominal CT scan. Her Bp is 120/80 , pulse 120/minute and respiratory rate was 30/min. Which ONE of the following is the appropriate immediate therapy?
srcNote: Source note (436 A Q23): The question was cancelled because more than 50% answered wrong. The course organizer told us the answer is Epinephrine. Source note (429 F Q19): anaphylaxic shock
expl: Urticaria + wheeze after contrast = anaphylaxis → epinephrine (IM). The question was cancelled because many answered wrong; the organizer confirmed epinephrine.

stem: Which of the following is a site of insertion for needle decompression for tension pneumothorax?
expl: Classic needle decompression: 2nd intercostal space, mid-clavicular line (ATLS 10th ed. prefers the 4th/5th ICS mid-axillary line in adults because the chest wall is thinner there).

why.C: Mid-axillary (not mid-clavicular) for the lateral approach.

stem: Which of the following is the most common site for venous cutdown to use in resuscitation of a 28 year-old male in hypovolemic shock due to abdominal blunt trauma?
expl: Venous cut-down: great saphenous vein anterior to the medial malleolus.

why.D: Small saphenous runs behind the lateral malleolus — not the standard.

stem: What is the best position for subclavian central line insertion?
expl: Trendelenburg (head-down) distends the subclavian/jugular veins and reduces the risk of air embolism; the head is turned away from the side of insertion.

why.A: Head turns away from the side.
why.B: Head turns away from the side.

stem: When inserting a chest tube which one of the following is done?

opts.t: A tube size of 12-14 Fr is commonly used for adults

expl: Chest-tube insertion is a sterile procedure under local anaesthesia; adult trauma tubes are large (28–32 Fr for haemothorax); CT isn't needed.

stem: Which of the following is most likely to be done during a nasogastric intubation?

opts.t: The tube is initially inserted superiorly into the nose
Auscultation is done to confirm the proper placement of the tube

expl: Source key B — classic bedside check: insufflate air and auscultate over the epigastrium (aspiration with pH testing and X-ray are more reliable). The tube is passed backwards along the nasal floor, not upwards.

stem: Nurse in the surgery ward called the surgical team to induce a Nasogastric tube. Why do you think ?

opts.t: For patient who has elective cholecystectomy

expl: NG tubes are inserted for GI bleeding (to assess/lavage), decompression (obstruction, ileus) and feeding. Not routine for elective cholecystectomy; contraindicated in nasal fracture.

why.B: The other year's key considered this an indication too.

stem: Patient had small laceration of his forehead, 5-0 prolene cutting suture were used. when should the suture be removed.
expl: Facial sutures are removed at 3–5 days; this version keyed "at least 2 days" (the other versions keyed 4–5 days).

why.B: Also within the face range (other version's key).

stem: Patient presented to ER with abdominal pain, and you have been called to insert NGT, Which one of the following is an indication for NGT?
expl: Source key A: in a perforated duodenal ulcer an NG tube decompresses the stomach and reduces peritoneal contamination. NGT is contraindicated in basal skull and maxillofacial fractures; it isn't needed for elective lap chole.

stem: a patient who had a single wound with one puncture in his forearm. Cleaning and debridement was done. What is the next step?
srcNote: (Skin, soft tissue, wound, and scars) Puncture wounds are never sutured duo to likelihood of infection (esp if duo to a bite)
expl: Puncture wounds (especially bites) are left open after cleaning and debridement because of the high infection risk; prophylactic oral antibiotics are given.

why.B: Never close a puncture wound primarily.
why.D: Not needed for a single clean-looking puncture.

stem: A patient presented with a 2cm*0.5 cm laceration on the forehead. How would you manage his injury after debridement of the wound?
expl: A clean, fresh facial laceration is closed by primary intention (well-vascularised face, best cosmetic result), without tension.

stem: Forehead suture removal should be done at?
srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patient)
expl: Face sutures out at 3–5 days → day 5.

stem: a young female pt underwent Haemorrhoidectomy under epidural anesthesia, complaining of headache. Which of the following is the last definitive management?
srcNote: (Practical Procedures and Investigation of Surgical Patients)
expl: The definitive ("last") treatment for persistent post-dural-puncture headache is an epidural blood patch.

stem: What is the longest acting local anesthesia?
srcNote: | (Practical Procedures & Investigation of Surgical Patients) (1.5-8 hours)
expl: Bupivacaine has the longest duration (≈ 2–8 h); lidocaine ≈ 1–2 h.

stem: how to confirm the placement of NGT? (Incomplete Q)
srcNote: | (Practical Procedures & Investigation of Surgical Patients) (I assume that he was asking about confirming the position of the tube (to confirm correct placement: free aspiration of gastric contents + auscultation in the epigastrium while 20 ml of air is insufflated)
expl: Bedside confirmation = aspirate gastric contents and check pH; an X-ray is the gold standard when aspiration fails.

stem: a 25 y/o male came to the ED presenting with a picture of right sided pneumothorax. The plan is to insert a chest tube. Which of the following would aid you in locating the site quickly? (Incomplete Q)
srcNote: , (Chest trauma) the Q was about the location of the tube (5th intercostal in the mid-to-anterior axillary line= nipple in males, inframammary line in females)
expl: The 5th intercostal space at the mid/anterior axillary line corresponds to the nipple level in men (inframammary fold in women).

stem: Central vein catheter sites
srcNote: (Practical Procedures & Investigation of Surgical Patients) The common sites of insertion of catheters into the superior vena cava are from the internal jugular vein in the neck, from the subclavian vein, or occasionally from a peripheral vein in the antecubital fossa.
expl: Central venous catheters reach the SVC from the internal jugular or subclavian veins, or the IVC from the femoral vein.
ansText: Internal jugular vein, subclavian vein, femoral vein (and a peripheral vein in the antecubital fossa = PICC). The only recalled option was "IJV and EJV" — the EJV is a peripheral vein, the IJV is the classic central site.

stem: Antiemetic (incomplete Q)
expl: Ondansetron (5-HT3 antagonist) is the standard antiemetic for post-operative nausea and vomiting. PPIs reduce acid; they are not antiemetics.

stem: 32 y\o man brought to the ER after involvement in a RTA. On examination he was dyspneic with severe maxillofacial injury. Which of the following urgent airway control method is appropriate?
expl: Severe maxillofacial injury with dyspnoea → oral/nasal intubation may be impossible or dangerous → surgical airway (cricothyroidotomy).

why.C: Often impossible with severe facial trauma.

stem: How many areas are assessed with FAST?
expl: FAST = 4 views: pericardial (subxiphoid), RUQ (hepatorenal), LUQ (splenorenal), pelvis. eFAST adds both hemithoraces.

stem: A 30 year old football player sustained head trauma and is unresponsive and snoring loudly. What is the best way to open his airway?

opts.t: Put the patient on his side

expl: Snoring = tongue obstructing the airway in an unconscious head-injured patient → jaw thrust (protects the C-spine).

stem: What is the most rapid way to gain access in an adult trauma with difficult peripheral intravenous access?
srcNote: (Trauma) Central venous cannulation is difficult and potentially hazardous in shocked hypovolemic patients, so if percutaneous access cannot be obtained, a surgical cut-down at the saphenofemoral junction is preferable, although more time-consuming. Intraosseous access to long bones in the adult is a viable alternative for initial resuscitation.Reference: Davidson 6th ed. ch. 7 p. 98
expl: When peripheral access fails in a shocked adult, intraosseous access is the fastest alternative (cut-down and central lines take longer).

stem: A 30-year-old football player sustained maxillofacial fracture. What is the best way to open his airway?

opts.t: Put the patient on his side

expl: With facial/head trauma, assume a C-spine injury: open the airway with a jaw thrust (no head tilt).

why.D: Recovery position doesn't secure the airway in trauma.

stem: the question was about a patient getting a lumbar puncture, what is the anatomical landmark that will indicate you’re in the right space?
expl: Source key D ("posterior superior iliac crest") — the intercristal (Tuffier's) line at L4 is the landmark for the L3/4–L4/5 spaces.

stem: In which of the following patients would performance of diagnostic peritoneal lavage is considered an absolute contraindication?

opts.t: Pregnant with hypotension after a blunt trauma
Expanding abdomen after a chest stab wound
Hypotension after car accident with previous abdominal surgery

srcNote: (Acute abdomen) (according to different sources, the only absolute contraindication to diagnostic peritoneal lavage is presence of the need to do exploratory laparotomy)
expl: The only absolute contraindication to DPL is an existing indication for laparotomy — an expanding abdomen after a stab wound needs the OR. Pregnancy and previous surgery are relative contraindications.

stem: Which one of the following can’t be seen by E-FAST?
expl: eFAST sees the pericardium, intraperitoneal fluid and pneumothorax/haemothorax, but not the retroperitoneum.

stem: A 20 y/o man was involved in a road traffic accident and found to be in a respiratory distress. Brought to the emergency department and he was intubated on bag valve mask. The anesthetic told you he has to use a lot of force ventilate the patient. On auscultation there is a reduced air entry on left side of the chest, trachea is deviated to the right.What is the most appropriate management option for this patient?

opts.t: Thoracostomy tube in the right 2nd intercostal space.
Thoracostomy tube in the left 2nd intercostal space.
Needle decompression on the left 2nd intercostal space.
Needle decompression on the right 2nd intercostal space.

expl: Hard to ventilate, reduced air entry on the LEFT and trachea deviated to the RIGHT → left tension pneumothorax → needle decompression on the left (2nd ICS MCL, or 4th–5th ICS in newer ATLS).

why.A: Wrong side, and a chest tube isn't the first step.

stem: Which ONE of the following is required after right subclavian central venous catheter insertion?
expl: After subclavian (or IJ) CVC insertion, a chest X-ray checks the tip position and excludes pneumothorax.

stem: Regarding inguinal hernia repair under local anesthesia, which of the following nerve is usually blocked?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) , Blocks of the ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerves may reduce the incidence of this chronic pain. Blocking the genital branch of genitofemoral nerve completes the nerve block for inguinal hernia surgeries. All these three nerves can be easily blocked under http://www.apicareonline.com/ultrasound-guided-hernia-blocks/
expl: Local-anaesthetic inguinal hernia repair blocks the ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric and genital branch of the genitofemoral nerves; of the choices only the iliohypogastric is involved.

stem: Which of the following is contraindicated when using local anesthetic drugs?

opts.t: Lidocaine with adrenaline in ingrowing toe nail surgery
Bupivacaine in analgesia of rib fracture
Lidocaine in repair of inguinal hernia

srcNote: (Practical Procedures & Investigation of Surgical Patients), due to the risk of ischemia
expl: Adrenaline with local anaesthetic is avoided in end-artery areas (fingers, toes, penis, ear) — risk of ischaemia/necrosis. The other uses are appropriate.

stem: Regarding nasogastric tube insertion, the nasal route should be avoided in which ONE OF the following conditions?

opts.t: Head injury with skull base fracture

expl: A skull-base fracture is a contraindication to nasal tubes (risk of intracranial passage) → pass the tube orally.

why.B: Relative caution, not an absolute contraindication.
why.D: Caution (risk of perforating the pouch), but not the keyed answer.

stem: Which ONE of the following is true regarding the appropriate site of insertion of chest tube pneumothorax ?
expl: Source key C (mid-axillary line, 6th ICS). The standard safe triangle is the 4th–5th ICS anterior/mid-axillary; of the choices given, mid-axillary is the right line.

stem: The chest tube for pneumothorax is inserted in:
expl: Chest tube → 5th ICS, mid-axillary line. 2nd ICS mid-clavicular is the needle-decompression site.

stem: chest tube:
expl: Chest tube → mid-axillary line, 5th ICS (safe triangle).

stem: Investigation of choice post subclavian central catheter is:
expl: After subclavian line insertion → chest X-ray to confirm tip position and exclude pneumothorax.

stem: common site for venous cut down during resuscitation is:
expl: The classic venous cut-down site is the great saphenous vein at the ankle (in front of the medial malleolus). The basilic vein at the elbow is an alternative.

stem: diagnostic peritoneal lavage all true except:
expl: Source key A (marked "??"). DPL is performed after an NG tube and Foley catheter (decompress stomach and bladder) through a small infra-umbilical incision. In ATLS it IS used for unexplained hypotension when FAST is unavailable, so the key is debated.

stem: After abdominal CT contrast 15y girl develop Urticaria, wheezing, normal BP, respiratory
expl: Urticaria + wheezing after contrast = anaphylaxis → epinephrine. (IM is the usual route; this old key said IV.)

stem: Central line complication (they probably mean which one of the following is not a complication of central line)
expl: Central line complications: pneumothorax, arterial puncture/hematoma, arrhythmia (guidewire), air embolism, infection, thrombosis. Convulsion is not one.

stem: ERCP NOT done in “incomplete Q”
expl: ERCP needs endoscopic access to the papilla; after gastrectomy with Billroth II/Roux-en-Y reconstruction, the papilla is hard or impossible to reach.

stem: Where to put the tip of subclavian central line catheter insertion?
expl: The tip of a subclavian line should sit in the lower SVC, at the level of the carina on CXR.
